Vanessa: Sulking is not going to make him come back! You will feel better soon. Next week you will have completely forgotten him!
Sally: I had no idea he was married. Oh well, you're right. At this time tomorrow, we will be watching the sunset on a beach.
Vanessa: Being on a plane is so cramped. Do you think they will bump us up to first class?
Sally: I hope they do. I am going to pray that they do. When we arrive in Jamaica, it will be hot and sunny. By this time tomorrow, we will have checked into our hotel room and eaten spicy Jamaican food for dinner.

Vanessa: I hope so. I have to pack. Are you bringing sunscreen because I'd rather not. I want to pack as lightly as I can.
Sally: The Caves is the most stunning resort. We'll sit on the cliffs, we'll go to the spa ... Actually, we are both having a massage the day after tomorrow. The spa is open every day from 9:00 to 5:00, so, I've already booked them.
Vanessa: Snorkeling is the thing I really have to do! The last time I tried it, an aggressive man got drunk on the boat and picked a fight with the captain. We had to turn around and come back. They refunded our money, but I had to go back home the next day.

Sally: Let's hope there aren't any saboteurs on our holiday.
Vanessa: Feeling relaxed is all I care about. Did you know that in two days I will have lived in the US for four years? Hopefully I will be living here for another four! I will have worked at Bistro 88 for two years. Isn't that mind-blowing?
Sally: Plus, next week I will have been in this world for just over a quarter of a century.

The Future Continuous and Future Perfect Tenses vs. Regular Future Tenses
You use the Future Continuous tense to express actions that occur in the future.

For example:
I will be working at 4 p.m. tomorrow.
The person will start work at some point in the future and be working at 4 p.m. It is not clear when the person will stop working.

The structure of the Future Continuous is:
Subject + will + be + verb -ing
Hopefully I will be living here for another four years!

You use the Future Perfect tense to express actions that will be finished at a specific time in the future.
For example:
I can call you in the early afternoon. I will have arrived in Houston by then.
The movie will start at 8 p.m. You will get to the movie theater at 8:15 p.m. By the time you get to the movie theater, the movie will have started.

The structure of the Future Perfect tense is:
Subject + will + have + past participle
I will have worked at Bistro 88 for two years.
Look at the chart for a comparison of the other tenses used to talk about the future.

Gerunds
When a verb ends in -ing, it may be a present participle or it may be a gerund.
When you use a verb + ing form more like a verb or an adjective, it is usually a present participle:

Vanessa is shopping.
The movie is exciting.
When we use a verb in -ing form more like a noun, it is usually a gerund:
Shopping is fun.
You should think of a gerund as a verb in noun form.
Like nouns, gerunds can be the subject of a sentence:
Sulking is not going to make him come back!
Gerunds are sometimes called "verbal nouns".
Feeling relaxed is all I care about.
Snorkeling is the thing I really have to do!

engenn9le14ob01aud03

to intentionally start an argument or physical altercation
(verb)

engenn9le14ob01aud04

to give money back after a service or product that was considered unsatisfactory
(verb)
